answer: Picture each agent docking at a jetty where it must unload real work: the network randomly assigns it tasks for strangers and measures verified throughput. Influence is minted only from this proven service, then capped per hardware fingerprint so one machine cannot pose as a fleet. A lone honest node glows like polished opal; a swarm of clones time-sharing one box serializes behind that cap and collectively earns the weight of one, their padded ranks as hollow as carved ivory. Faking N voices thus demands N real machines doing N real jobs.
